newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Lee Hoi-chang, Chairman of the ruling New Korea Party, gave a news conference. He said all political practices, including elections, political funding and party operations should be throughly reformed.
- Some 134 children died of starvation in North Korea, said Unicef spokesman.

- The South Korean government plans to buy 500,000 tonnes of rice from Japan as aid to North Korea if it attends the four-way peace talks. Seoul has already informed Tokyo of its intentions and will finalise details when the South Korean Foreign Minister visits his counter part in Japan on Monday.
- The nations's leading aerospace companies have agreed in principle to sign a contract for joint development with Europe's AIR to build middle size passenger planes, industry sources said.
- A Hanbo Group founder Chun Tae-soo's chief accountant neither confirmed nor denied a news report that he had delivered money to some politicians at the instruction of Chung.

- Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui told a high-level U.S. Congressional delegation that Taipei would shelve a plan to ship nuclear waste to North Korea if it doesn't meet safety requirements, a government official said.
- Korea's automakers are expected to see a steep decline in plant operationg rates this year due to increased capacity and reduced working hours at Hyundai.
